items.title: README: explain removing secrets and synchronising removals
items.body:
## The problem

The README quick start shows how to set, import, read and share secrets, but does not show `sotto rm`. A reader has no removal walkthrough explaining which environment is affected, when confirmation happens, or how a local removal reaches other devices.

Add a short guide to the existing command so readers can remove an obsolete secret without guessing at those details.

## Proposed approach

Add a concise secret-removal section near the CLI quick start. Use a clearly synthetic name such as `DEMO_OBSOLETE_KEY`, and explain local removal followed by optional server synchronisation. This is documentation of current behaviour, with no changes to deletion or confirmation policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Show a named removal and a consistent environment-specific sequence, for example `sotto --env staging rm DEMO_OBSOLETE_KEY` followed by `sotto --env staging push`. Explain that removal affects the selected environment, remains local until pushed, and reaches another device when it pulls that environment. Server synchronisation requires login.
- [ ] Explain interactive behaviour: omitting the name opens the secret picker; removal normally asks for confirmation, with No as the default; declining or cancelling leaves the secret unchanged. `--yes` / `-y` skips the confirmation, but does not skip an omitted-name picker or any required unlock prompt.
- [ ] Explain non-interactive behaviour accurately: a name is required, and a named removal does not ask for confirmation even without `--yes`. The picker/confirmation require interactive stdin, stdout and stderr, a non-dumb terminal, and CI not being active.
- [ ] State that removal hides the secret from ordinary reads/listings and retains version history; it is not secure erasure or revocation of the credential at its external provider. Keep recovery instructions with the history/rollback documentation rather than adding a second recovery walkthrough here.
- [ ] Keep README translations aligned with `CONTRIBUTING.md`, use British English and plain hyphens, verify command examples against current source/help, and run `scripts/check-readme-i18n`.

## Evidence and starting points

Source-inspected on main `d4928a53c93a93df9d9d7c95c67795b4bd8875b2` in a clean checkout on macOS arm64:

- [README](https://github.com/getsotto/sotto/blob/d4928a53c93a93df9d9d7c95c67795b4bd8875b2/README.md): no `sotto rm` example.
- [CLI](https://github.com/getsotto/sotto/blob/d4928a53c93a93df9d9d7c95c67795b4bd8875b2/crates/cli/src/main.rs): `Command::Rm`, its dispatch arm and `effective_config`.
- [Prompts](https://github.com/getsotto/sotto/blob/d4928a53c93a93df9d9d7c95c67795b4bd8875b2/crates/cli/src/prompts.rs): `can_prompt`, `preflight_secret_name`, `select_secret_key` and `confirm_removal`.
- [Vault removal](https://github.com/getsotto/sotto/blob/d4928a53c93a93df9d9d7c95c67795b4bd8875b2/crates/cli/src/vault.rs): `delete` and the existing deletion tests.
- [Sync](https://github.com/getsotto/sotto/blob/d4928a53c93a93df9d9d7c95c67795b4bd8875b2/crates/cli/src/remote/sync.rs): `push`, `diff` and `push_provisions_and_round_trips_through_pull`, whose final scenario covers deletion reaching another device.

This is a documentation gap established by source inspection. The referenced tests were read, not executed for this issue; no local or remote secret was removed. Open/closed issues and open PRs were checked for overlap. #591 covers restoring earlier versions and #558 documents environment selection/copying; neither provides a secret-removal guide.

## Where this lives

Docs / copy. Suitable for a first contribution with source checking. Follow `CONTRIBUTING.md`, including DCO sign-off (`git commit -s`).
